Done. The Deployment is now applied under `apps/v1` and fully converged.

## What the cluster actually serves

`kubectl api-versions` shows the cluster (server v1.37.0) serves only `apps/v1` from that group. I confirmed the legacy groups are genuinely unserved:

| API version | Status |
|---|---|
| `apps/v1` | served |
| `apps/v1beta1` | NOT served |
| `apps/v1beta2` | NOT served |
| `extensions/v1beta1` | NOT served |

## The change made

A single-field change: `apiVersion: apps/v1beta1` → `apiVersion: apps/v1`. Everything else was already valid for `apps/v1`, so no other field was touched. Notably, `apps/v1` makes `spec.selector` **required** (it was optional in `apps/v1beta1`), and the handed-over manifest already supplied `matchLabels: {app: app}` matching the pod template — I verified this with `kubectl explain deployment.spec.selector --api-version=apps/v1` rather than assuming. No labels, defaults, strategy, or port settings were altered.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: nginx:1.31.5
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 80
```

`kubectl apply -n legacy-app -f` → `deployment.apps/app created`.

## Verification (fresh observations)

The originally reported symptom — the cluster rejecting the resource — is gone, and the requested outcome is confirmed directly:

- **Served version accepted**: live object reports `apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment`.
- **Replicas match exactly**: `replicas=3 updated=3 ready=3 available=3`, `observedGeneration=1` equals `generation=1`. `kubectl rollout status` returned "successfully rolled out"; the 3 pods are `1/1 Running` with `RESTARTS 0`.
- **Image is genuinely the intended one**, read from the running container status rather than the spec: all three pods report `nginx:1.31.5` with the same `imageID` digest `sha256:05b8cb60…`, `ready=true`. Events show `Successfully pulled image "nginx:1.31.5"` — so this reference really resolves, no `ImagePullBackOff`.
- **Preserved identity**: name `app`, label `app=app` on both the Deployment and every pod, port `http`/80, selector `app=app`.
- **Actually functional**, not just "looks healthy": `curl` inside a pod against port 80 returned `http_code=200`.
- **No warnings**: `type=Warning` events in the namespace returned no resources.

One note for the handover: I wrote the corrected manifest to `/tmp/app-deployment.yaml` inside this sandbox only — update the team's source file in their repo so a future apply doesn't reintroduce `apps/v1beta1`.

message.content:
Done. The Deployment is now applied under `apps/v1` and fully converged.

## What the cluster actually serves

`kubectl api-versions` shows the cluster (server v1.37.0) serves only `apps/v1` from that group. I confirmed the legacy groups are genuinely unserved:

| API version | Status |
|---|---|
| `apps/v1` | served |
| `apps/v1beta1` | NOT served |
| `apps/v1beta2` | NOT served |
| `extensions/v1beta1` | NOT served |

## The change made

A single-field change: `apiVersion: apps/v1beta1` → `apiVersion: apps/v1`. Everything else was already valid for `apps/v1`, so no other field was touched. Notably, `apps/v1` makes `spec.selector` **required** (it was optional in `apps/v1beta1`), and the handed-over manifest already supplied `matchLabels: {app: app}` matching the pod template — I verified this with `kubectl explain deployment.spec.selector --api-version=apps/v1` rather than assuming. No labels, defaults, strategy, or port settings were altered.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: nginx:1.31.5
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 80
```

`kubectl apply -n legacy-app -f` → `deployment.apps/app created`.

## Verification (fresh observations)

The originally reported symptom — the cluster rejecting the resource — is gone, and the requested outcome is confirmed directly:

- **Served version accepted**: live object reports `apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment`.
- **Replicas match exactly**: `replicas=3 updated=3 ready=3 available=3`, `observedGeneration=1` equals `generation=1`. `kubectl rollout status` returned "successfully rolled out"; the 3 pods are `1/1 Running` with `RESTARTS 0`.
- **Image is genuinely the intended one**, read from the running container status rather than the spec: all three pods report `nginx:1.31.5` with the same `imageID` digest `sha256:05b8cb60…`, `ready=true`. Events show `Successfully pulled image "nginx:1.31.5"` — so this reference really resolves, no `ImagePullBackOff`.
- **Preserved identity**: name `app`, label `app=app` on both the Deployment and every pod, port `http`/80, selector `app=app`.
- **Actually functional**, not just "looks healthy": `curl` inside a pod against port 80 returned `http_code=200`.
- **No warnings**: `type=Warning` events in the namespace returned no resources.

One note for the handover: I wrote the corrected manifest to `/tmp/app-deployment.yaml` inside this sandbox only — update the team's source file in their repo so a future apply doesn't reintroduce `apps/v1beta1`.
